Power & Grid.why: Transformers, switchgear, gas turbines, fuel cells, SMRs — where the buildout actually hits the physical world. Power is now scarcer than chips: a ~2,600 GW interconnection backlog (median ~5-year wait) and 30–40-month transformer lead times make this the single most binding constraint in the stack. GE Vernova's gas-turbine backlog hit ~100 GW / $176B with pricing up ~300% in three years.

Compute & Silicon.why: Where capital is most concentrated and most exposed. The EDA duopoly (Synopsys/Cadence) and custom-ASIC design (Broadcom/Marvell, growing ~45%/yr vs ~16% for GPUs) are durable moats. Merchant AI accelerators and frontier labs are not — and the neocloud model now runs on circular financing (Nvidia takes equity → neoclouds buy Nvidia GPUs → GPU-collateralised debt), which holds only while AI demand keeps compounding.

Memory & Storage.why: Now ~63% of an AI chip's bill of materials — bigger than the logic die (~13%) and tighter than the GPU itself. An HBM/DRAM/NAND triopoly (SK Hynix, Samsung, Micron) running 70%+ margins, sold out of 2026 HBM with 2027 largely booked. DRAM contract prices rose 90%+ in a single quarter. The scarcest, highest-margin layer in the whole stack — and the one the map was missing.

Materials & Chemicals.why: Quiet near-monopolies. GOES electrical steel (Cleveland-Cliffs is the sole North American producer), EUV photoresists, high-purity silicon wafers, InP / GaAs substrates for photonics, titanium alloys for gas-turbine generators, and the HBM consumables (Ajinomoto ~98% of ABF film, Namics sole-source MR-MUF) that a handful of Japanese suppliers control outright.

Connectivity & Photonics.why: The whole 'moving-bits' half of the data center: switch silicon (Broadcom, Marvell), the scale-up (NVLink/UALink) and scale-out (InfiniBand vs Ethernet) fabrics, 800G/1.6T optical modules, plus subsea fibre and hyperscaler dark-fibre IRUs. A GB200 NVL72 rack is ~2 miles of copper and thousands of optical links; networking is the fastest-growing capex line at both Nvidia and Broadcom.

Construction & Labor.why: Skilled electricians, mechanical contractors, transmission specialists. A 1 GW campus needs 3,000–4,000 electricians at peak; the IBEW pipeline cannot supply at AI cadence. MEP contractors now turn down work — pricing power is structural.

Cooling & Thermal.why: GB200/GB300 racks at 120+ kW exceed air-cooling limits. Microsoft made liquid cooling the default for its Maia accelerators; Nvidia Vera Rubin is designed for 45°C hot-water cooling. Air→liquid retrofit cycle is forced, not optional.

Fab & Test Equipment.why: The picks and shovels behind every chip. Litho tools (ASML for EUV, AMAT/LRCX for deposition and etch, KLA for inspection) print the transistors; test handlers (Teradyne, AEHR) prove the wafers and packages survive. A narrow oligopoly the entire foundry universe runs through — and the part of the stack still being repriced.

Software & Apps.why: The demand layer. Enterprise AI integration is where model output becomes revenue, and where the trillion-dollar capex bill ultimately gets paid for. ServiceNow leads the front-office integration race; multiple-X upside remains even with the name in the open.
